claim_boundary.scope: repository authority architecture, projection integrity, and audit interpretation

formal_flow: HUMAN -> GOVERNED_JSON -> GOVERNED_EXTRACTION -> DATABASE -> RUNTIME -> VALIDATION -> MARKDOWN
core_rule: Human input proposes. Governed admission authorizes. The database governs agents. Validation tests admitted state. Markdown reports validated state.
non_circularity_rule: Human-authored source material entering the pipeline and generated Markdown leaving the pipeline are distinct artifact roles even when both use Markdown syntax.

authority_rule.human_facing_ssot_qualification: Markdown is authoritative for human consumption only to the extent that it is a current validated projection of canonical database state.
authority_rule.forbidden_interpretation: Markdown and the database must not be treated as co-equal competing operational authorities.

canonical_flow.role: originates mathematical intent, definitions, corrections, and governance decisions
encodes human intent as a structured proposal or change packet
validates, normalizes, resolves identifiers, preserves provenance, and determines admissibility
stores admitted canonical state for agent reasoning and governed execution
executes and reasons only from admitted database state
tests canonical state, runtime behavior, evidence, invariants, and projection consistency
renders validated canonical state for human inspection

conservation_rules.rule: No human-authored source becomes agent authority without governed admission.
No generated Markdown may independently modify canonical database state.
Every admitted canonical object must preserve provenance to its governed submission and human source.
Every generated Markdown claim must resolve to canonical database object identifiers and versions.
Validation may approve, reject, qualify, or report canonical state but may not silently rewrite it.
Runtime agents must not infer authority from file location, prose confidence, document title, or SSOT wording alone.
Projection drift is a synchronization defect, not evidence that Markdown and the database are competing authorities.
A human-facing SSOT must identify the canonical database snapshot from which it was generated.

implementation_note: This architecture defines the intended authority pipeline. If current database coverage is partial, agents must report the gap and fall back under governed rules without treating Markdown as a competing operational SSOT.
